deviceDetail.typeAutoHint: Detected automatically from the router hostname and MAC vendor.
deviceDetail.osWeak: OS {{os}} is only an estimate{{weak}} — passive detection (TTL/hostname) cannot confirm it without access to the device.
deviceDetail.randomMac: The MAC is randomized (private), so the vendor cannot be read from the OUI.
deviceDetail.typeUnknownTitle: The type could not be determined automatically.
deviceDetail.typeUnknown: This device sends no DHCP hostname and uses a randomized MAC, so there is no data that identifies it as an Apple device (iPhone/iPad/Mac), phone, laptop, or anything else. If you know what it is, pick a type above — your choice is saved and will not be overwritten by the next scan.
deviceDetail.brandHint: Pick a brand logo if automatic detection is wrong. The choice is saved permanently for this device.
deviceDetail.brandAutoHint: The logo follows the device's OUI vendor and hostname.
deviceDetail.typeSaveError: Failed to save the device type
deviceDetail.ifaceSaveError: Failed to save the device SSID
deviceDetail.unkickRuleMissing: No matching rule was found on the router (it may have been removed manually). ARP has been stopped.
deviceDetail.roamWarning: This device has been seen on {{targeted}} SSIDs, but only {{blocked}} were blocked. If the device moves to a failed SSID, the block does not apply — repeat the kick while the device is connected to that SSID.
deviceDetail.kickHelp: The permanent block lives on the router (WLAN Advanced → Access Control Rule): the device cannot connect again until you press Stop kick. The instant drop uses ARP spoofing and may not work on every device — especially modern iOS/Android devices that tolerate ARP spoofing.
deviceDetail.fallbackWarning: The router does not report an AP for this device, so the default is used. If the device is actually on another SSID, the block will not apply — pick an AP below.
deviceDetail.apHint: An Access Control rule only applies on the selected AP. A wrong choice makes the block fail silently.
deviceDetail.dataUnavailable: Per-device data usage totals are not available on this router. ZTE F670L firmware only exposes the instantaneous rates (bps) above — there is no cumulative per-client byte counter anywhere in the admin panel. This backend also runs outside the gateway path, so netdash cannot count other devices' traffic from the network.
deviceDetail.connectionHistorySub: Online/offline status from connect and disconnect transitions
deviceDetail.notEnoughHistory: Not enough history to draw a chart yet.
deviceDetail.deleteBody: Use this only for old, test, or ghost entries that no longer exist on the network. This device's connection and kick history will also be deleted and cannot be recovered.
deviceDetail.deleteSelf: This device runs the backend, so it cannot be deleted.
deviceDetail.deleteGateway: The gateway cannot be deleted because scans and kicks need it.
deviceDetail.deleteKicked: Stop kicking this device before deleting it.
deviceDetail.deletePermanent: This is permanent. The device will reappear if it is still connected to the network on the next scan.

speedtest.title: Speedtest
speedtest.subtitle: Manual — never runs automatically
speedtest.help: One click runs download and then upload in sequence. A test uses the full bandwidth for about 10–30 seconds and never runs automatically.
speedtest.helpShort: Download and upload run in sequence in one test.
speedtest.pingNote: Ping and jitter are measured by the test engine. When the official Speedtest CLI (Ookla) is available, the figures match speedtest.net; the fallback mode uses median TCP connect time to the same server.
speedtest.fallbackWarning: This result used the fallback speedtest-cli engine because the official Speedtest CLI (Ookla) is not installed. Server selection and throughput figures may be less accurate. Install the official `speedtest` client or set NETDASH_SPEEDTEST_BIN for speedtest.net-equivalent results.
speedtest.scrollHint: Swipe the table sideways to see every column.
speedtest.deleteAllConfirm: Delete all speedtest history? This action cannot be undone.
speedtest.publicIpPending: The public IP appears when the first test starts.
speedtest.serverHint: Pick a server manually or leave it automatic.
speedtest.serverLoadError: Could not load the server list. The test can still use the closest server.
speedtest.serverSelectedHint: The selected server is used when a test starts.
speedtest.serverAutoHint: The closest server is selected automatically when a test starts.

settings.title: Settings
settings.saved: Settings saved. A rescan has been started.
settings.interfaceHint: In use: {{name}} ({{ip}}). Choose automatic to let the app decide.
settings.noRawSocket: The backend does not have raw socket access. ARP scan and ARP spoofing cannot run, so devices that are actually online may appear offline and kicks will not block traffic. On Linux run the command below and restart the backend. On Windows run as Administrator and install Npcap.
settings.rawSocketOk: The backend has raw socket access — ARP scan and spoofing can run.
settings.defaultScapy: scapy default (risky; ignored by the app)
settings.adapterNote: This app always sends through the adapter that holds your local IP, not scapy's default. On machines with VMware/VirtualBox, scapy's default may point at a virtual adapter so frames never reach the LAN.
settings.kickMethodHint: Router = block the MAC through Access Control (recommended, works on iOS/Android). ARP = legacy spoofing (fallback, requires Administrator).
settings.defaultSsidHint: Used for Access Control rules, e.g. DEV.WIFI.AP6 = the 6th SSID. Check the router under WLAN → SSID number.
settings.routerEnvEmpty: backend/.env exists but NETDASH_ROUTER_USER/PASS are empty in it.
settings.routerEnvMissing: The backend/.env file does not exist — create it with NETDASH_ROUTER_USER, NETDASH_ROUTER_PASS, and NETDASH_ROUTER_URL, then restart the backend.
settings.gatewayMacHint: Kicking needs the gateway MAC. Leave empty only when the gateway is detected automatically.
settings.kickDurationHint: Stops automatically as a safety measure
settings.whitelistHint: One MAC per line. These devices can never be kicked.
settings.ouiHint: Leave empty to use the bundled IEEE database (~40k entries, offline).
settings.languageHint: The choice is saved in this browser.
settings.displayNameHint: Shown in the account header. Leave empty to use the username.
settings.usernameHint: 3-32 characters: letters, numbers, dot, underscore, or hyphen.
settings.networkProfilesHint: Every network ever detected keeps its own devices and history.
settings.profilesEmpty: No network profile yet. Run a scan to detect the current network.
settings.resetOnlyActive: Reset is only available for the active network. Other networks stay untouched.
settings.resetBody: Every device, connection event, and block log for this network will be deleted, then the network is rescanned from scratch.
settings.resetWarning: This cannot be undone. Other network profiles are not affected.
settings.resetConfirmLabel: Type the network name to confirm
settings.resetConfirmHint: Type exactly "{{name}}" then press the reset button.
settings.resetNameMismatch: The network name does not match. Type '{{name}}' to confirm.
settings.resetDone: Network {{name}} was reset and is being rescanned.
settings.scanHint: Subnet, interface, and network scan interval.
settings.kickHint: How devices are blocked when kick is used.
settings.vendorHint: OUI database used for device vendor names.
settings.accountHint: The name shown in the header and your login credentials.
settings.diagnosticsHint: Raw-socket status and the adapter actually in use.
settings.saveHint: Scan and kick changes take effect after saving.
